sheet-2-1.description: The right half of sheet 2 shows the western business and railroad district of Jamesburg at 100 feet to the inch, between Gatzmer Avenue and Stockton Avenue, from Mott Avenue at the top to Front at the bottom. It is separated from the left half by a heavy vertical line and has its own compass rose; the street grid is drawn square to the page with north turned about 30 degrees to the right. The Pennsylvania Railroad lines (the Camden and Amboy and the Freehold and Jamesburg branches) and the Jamesburg station yard curve through the middle of the part, with freight sheds, platforms and a hotel beside them. Along Gatzmer Avenue and Railroad Avenue stand lumber and coal yards, among them Perrine and Buckelew's lumber yard and builders' supplies at the top and the B. D. Davison lumber company with its cement block plant near Front, the Stonaker and Harvey grain elevator and feed mill near Grand, a motion picture house on Grand and a mix of dwellings, stores and auto garages. The blocks between Sherman and Lincoln Avenue east of Gatzmer are closely built with dwellings and small shops. Half Acre Road enters from the left between Lincoln Avenue and Hooker. Water pipes of four and six inches run in the streets. The part adjoins sheet 3 to the right along Stockton Avenue and sheet 4 at the bottom along Front.
notes: Railroad Avenue here is West Railroad Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Gatzmer Avenue / Grand was rejected by the fit (8.6 m); Gatzmer Avenue / West Railroad Avenue does not correspond to a drawn junction (16.6 m).

Sheet 2, 100 ft, two parts split by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (right half): Gatzmer Av to Stockton Av, Mott Av to Front, railroad yard. Part 2 (left half): Gatzmer Av north of the railroad to the Bordentown & Amboy Turnpike, own north arrow; anchored on one junction.

sheet-2-2.description: The left half of sheet 2 shows the north-western edge of Jamesburg at 100 feet to the inch: Gatzmer Avenue running north from the Pennsylvania Railroad crossing, where it passes under a concrete viaduct near Mott Avenue, to the Bordentown and Amboy Turnpike. It is drawn with its own north arrow, separated from the right half by a heavy vertical line, and the land is mostly large open lots. Near the railroad stands the Chamberlain and Barclay feed, hay, straw and potato warehouse with its hay barn, stable and sheds; a handful of dwellings line Gatzmer Avenue between the railroad and the turnpike. Beyond the turnpike the Jamesburg and Van Derhoof Shop Road runs diagonally to the upper left, lined with scattered dwellings and outbuildings, and Rhode Hill Road branches off to the upper right. R. A. Bennett's saw mill, I. S. Bennett's mill and a former bonded warehouse lie between these roads near the top. The dash-dot borough limits line crosses the top of the part and runs down its middle. Block numbers 7 to 12 are printed on the large lots. The part was placed from a single detected junction, Gatzmer Avenue and Mott Avenue, with the scale assumed and the rotation taken from the lines measured there, so its far end at the turnpike is uncertain by tens of metres.
notes: Bordentown & Amboy Turnpike is Bordentown Turnpike in OpenStreetMap; the junction with Gatzmer Avenue has been realigned (Browns Hall Road and Dayton Road meet it today).
Rhode Hill Road is probably today's Rhode Hall Road, which now leaves Browns Hall Road about 200 m north of the turnpike.
Placed from one detected point plus a derived point (scale 4.0 px/ft from the config, rotation from the measured lines): low confidence away from the railroad.

Sheet 2, 100 ft, two parts split by a heavy vertical line. Part 1 (right half): Gatzmer Av to Stockton Av, Mott Av to Front, railroad yard. Part 2 (left half): Gatzmer Av north of the railroad to the Bordentown & Amboy Turnpike, own north arrow; anchored on one junction.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the northern residential district of Jamesburg, drawn at 100 feet to the inch with the street grid set square to the page and north turned roughly 30 degrees to the right. Stockton Avenue runs down the left edge beside the railroad, with Stevens Avenue and McKnight Avenue parallel to it across the middle of the sheet. The cross streets, from the top, are Sheridan, Sherman, Lincoln Avenue, Sedgwick Avenue, Hooker, Vine and Augusta, and Helmetta Road cuts diagonally from the lower centre to the right edge, where it meets Lincoln Avenue and Sherman near the borough line. The blocks between Stockton and McKnight are closely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and their auto sheds; St. James Hall, a frame hall with a stage, stands on Lincoln Avenue at Stevens, and a few stores and small shops sit along Railroad Avenue in the lower left corner, where the tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad curve through the sheet. East of McKnight Avenue the blocks are only partly built up, and the upper part of the sheet beyond Sheridan is open land crossed by the dashed borough limit line, with only a few scattered buildings. Four-inch water pipes are drawn in most streets and fire hydrants are marked at the main corners, with a fire alarm box at Stevens Avenue and Lincoln Avenue. Block numbers run from 5 to 97 and house numbers are given along every frontage. The sheet joins sheet 2 on the left along Stockton Avenue and sheet 4 at the bottom along Augusta.
notes: Sedgwick Avenue is Sedwick Street and East Sedwick Street in OpenStreetMap.
Sheridan, Sherman and Hooker are Sheridan Street, Sherman Street (East Sherman Street east of Helmetta Road) and Hooker Street today.
Railroad Avenue here is West Railroad Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Sheet 3, 100 ft (pilot). North side: Stockton, Stevens, McKnight; Sheridan, Sherman, Lincoln Av, Sedgwick Av, Hooker, Vine, Augusta; Helmetta Rd. Grid turned about 30 degrees from north.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the centre and south side of Jamesburg at 100 feet to the inch, with the grid turned about 40 degrees from north. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs down the middle of the sheet between Railroad Avenue on the west and Railroad Avenue on the east. West of the tracks lie Front, Harrison, Church and Willow, crossing Gatzmer Avenue, with the Presbyterian church on Church, closely built dwellings, and along Railroad Avenue a row of stores, a bowling alley, bakery, barber and the W. C. Crosby shirt factory and John Monahan's shirt and steam laundry near Buckelew Avenue. East of the tracks are Augusta, Franklin and Warren between Railroad Avenue and Stevens Avenue, with the public school at the top right and the Eastern Foundry Company, and Church continuing diagonally to the right edge. Buckelew Avenue runs diagonally across the lower half to a bridge over Manalapan Brook at the outlet of the lake, which fills the bottom of the sheet; south of it the Perrineville Avenue, Manalapan Boulevard, Lake View Boulevard and Scott frontage is laid out in narrow building lots, still mostly empty. In the lower right, beyond the brook, are the New Jersey Novelty Company shoe factory, the Jamesburg electric light and pumping station and dwellings along Matchaponix Avenue or Pergola Avenue, Buckelew Avenue, John and Emma.
notes: Old Buckelew Avenue west of the railroad is Forsgate Drive today; Buckelew Avenue south of the brook keeps its name.
Railroad Avenue is West Railroad Avenue and East Railroad Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Lake View Boulevard is probably Lakeview Avenue.

Gatzmer Avenue was left out of the fit: its five junctions carried residuals of 3.7 to 5.2 m against the rest of the sheet (fit LOO 4.0 m with it, 3.05 m without), so the western third of the sheet rests on extrapolation.

Sheet 4, 100 ft. Centre and south: Front, Harrison, Church, Willow either side of the railroad (Railroad Av west and east), Augusta, Franklin, Warren, Stevens Av; Buckelew Av (now Forsgate Dr), lake and Manalapan Brook. Gatzmer Av left out of the fit (3.7 to 5.2 m residuals).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the south-eastern edge of Jamesburg at 100 feet to the inch, turned about 60 degrees from north. Buckelew Avenue runs down the sheet from top to bottom, with John and Emma at the top, Lake, Forge and New crossing it, and Cherry a narrow street parallel to it between Emma and Lake. The lake and Manalapan Brook form the left edge, with the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Amboy) and its freight depot, the Jamesburg electric light and pumping station and a garage along the tracks near John. Most of the sheet is open land in large numbered blocks with scattered dwellings; houses cluster along Buckelew Avenue near Lake, Forge and New and along New towards the right edge. A second railroad crosses the right side of the sheet in a long curve. In the upper right Matchaponix Avenue or Pergola Avenue runs diagonally, with Duane and George and a tract of narrow building lots beyond it. The dash-dot borough limit line runs across the sheet near Forge and down the lower left. Block numbers 48 to 95 are printed on the large blocks.
notes: Matchaponix Avenue or Pergola Avenue is Pergola Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Lake, Forge, New, Cherry, John, Emma, Duane and George are Lake Street, Forge Street, New Street, Cherry Street, John Street, Emma Street, Duane Street and George Street today.
Sheet 5, 100 ft. South-east edge: Buckelew Av, John, Emma, Cherry, Lake, Forge, New; Matchaponix or Pergola Av, Duane, George; lake along the west edge. Drawn about 60 degrees from north.
